key_insight: This review shows that elderly-care OR research has evolved from static, deterministic optimization to dynamic, stochastic, and AI-assisted decision support, but still rarely translates operational gains into better patient outcomes.
engineering_relevance: The paper informs healthcare systems engineering by identifying where routing, staffing, and scheduling tools can be extended into integrated, patient-centered decision frameworks across hospital and community care.
method: Thematic review of 30 seminal studies in OR and elderly care
Literature grouped into home healthcare operations, polypharmacy management, and clinical chronotherapy
Conceptual framework proposed for multi-level, digitally enabled decision-making
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a thematic review of 30 studies and synthesizes methodological trends rather than presenting new experimental data or a quantitative benchmark evaluation.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is that process optimization alone may not yield measurable clinical benefit without human-centered design and stronger links between operational and health outcomes.
paper_title: From Operations to Elderly Care Outcomes: A Thematic Review of Industrial Engineering and Decision-Support Approaches
